method: Hall's condition via minimum degree over the WHOLE action space
argument: for an S-set of size k, |O_i| >= deg(s_i)-(k-1); min|O_i| >= k satisfies Hall for every subset; hence deg(c) >= 2k-1 for all c proves every S-set of size <= k is perfectly matchable
tier_note: relaxation tiers are cumulative, so the most permissive tier's match set is the union over all tiers

WITHDRAWAL.why_it_was_wrong: The claim was computed from the S-sets the rehearsal actually produced, and every one of those 50 sets contained FOUR ids because the stand-in selector was called with k=4. A result about 4-element sets was reported under a name asserting 8. Sampled or first/last-k sets are probes; they are not a universal proof.
WITHDRAWAL.corrected_status: OPEN -- not universally proven, and NOT disproven either
WITHDRAWAL.what_is_now_proven: Hall's condition gives a SUFFICIENT test over the whole action space: if every candidate's admissible-control degree is >= 2k-1, then EVERY S-set of size <= k is perfectly matchable. Measured over all 50 exposed-50 universes, the minimum degree is 1, so this test proves set-level feasibility only up to k = 1, and k = 2 on the 34 fixtures whose minimum degree is 3.
WITHDRAWAL.what_is_NOT_claimed: That K=8 is INFEASIBLE. Hall's minimum-degree test is sufficient, not necessary: a low minimum degree means the universal proof fails, not that a particular 8-set has no perfect matching. Feasibility for any GIVEN set is still decided exactly, by the maximum-matching routine in control_coverage.set_level_feasibility.
WITHDRAWAL.how_to_close_it: Either raise the minimum degree over the action space (without shrinking the space or relaxing support thresholds, neither of which is permitted), or replace the universal claim with a per-selection check: run set_level_feasibility on the ACTUAL submitted S-set at freeze time and record the result per fixture.
